probes.question: A charger warms up as it works. Where does that heat energy come from?
options: It is converted from electrical energy
It is absorbed from the air

probes.question: True or false: Joule's law says heating power equals resistance times the square of the current.

image.alt: A black laptop AC power adapter with its cable coiled beside it on a white background.

body.claim: A warm charger is not losing energy for nothing: some of it is being transformed into heat.
body.why: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed or transferred. Current through any conductor produces heat, with heating power equal to the resistance times the square of the current. In older adapters the losses in the transformer and regulator were considerable, and significant power was dissipated as heat even with no load.
